deck_title: Day 001 — Operational Guide: What Aviation Does

slides.title: Aviation as an Interconnected System of Systems
slides.subtitle: Beyond the aluminum tube: Moving across sovereign borders and managed airspace
slides.key_takeaway: A flight is never an isolated technical event; it is the physical manifestation of international treaties, national sovereignty, commercial investment, and operational control.
bullets: Civil aviation operates across sovereign borders, physical movement surfaces, and 3D managed airspace.
Governed internationally by ICAO Doc 7300 (Chicago Convention 1944) and EASA Basic Regulation (EU) 2018/1139.
Establishes the Day 1 baseline: An intricate web of ground infrastructure, airworthiness, air traffic separation, and human control.
slides.technical_callout: System Topology: Convergence of ICAO Annexes (6, 11, 14) and national regulatory frameworks.
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome to Day 001 of the Aviation 365 curriculum. Today we establish that aviation is not just an airline ticket or an aircraft in flight, but a complex, highly regulated system of systems.

slides.title: Core Functions: Commerce, Lifeline Connectivity, and Public Service
slides.subtitle: Performing critical functions that no other transportation mode can duplicate
slides.key_takeaway: While air transport accounts for less than 1% of global freight tonnage, it carries over 35% of global trade by economic value.
bullets: High-Value Global Commerce: Just-in-time logistics, pharmaceuticals, human organs, microchips, and AOG aircraft spares.
Strategic Public Service: Lifeline connectivity for island archipelagos and northern communities when surface transport fails.
Public Service Obligations (PSO): Government-subsidized routes under EU Regulation (EC) 1008/2008 and US EAS for social and strategic cohesion.
Emergency Services: Aerial firefighting, search and rescue (SAR, ICAO Annex 12), and rapid humanitarian disaster response.
slides.technical_callout: Economic Multipliers: Direct, indirect, induced, and catalytic value layers across the global network.
slides.speaker_notes: Aviation drives global supply chains. It carries high-value cargo and serves as a vital lifeline for remote communities via Public Service Obligations.

slides.title: The Air Connectivity Index (ACI) & Economic Value
slides.subtitle: Quantifying economic integration, hub multipliers, and lifeline transport economics
slides.key_takeaway: Connectivity measures how deeply an aerodrome is integrated into the global network, weighted by frequency, aircraft capacity, and hub multipliers.
bullets: Direct ($V_{	ext{direct}}$), Indirect ($V_{	ext{indirect}}$), Induced ($V_{	ext{induced}}$), and Catalytic ($V_{	ext{catalytic}}$) value layers.
Mathematical Formulation: Weighted Air Connectivity Score (Ci) factoring flight frequency (Fij), seat capacity (Sij), and flight time (Tij).
Destination Hub Multipliers (Whub): Global Tier-1 Mega Hubs (2.0), Regional Hubs (1.4), and Spoke Non-Hubs (1.0).
PSO Economics: Sustaining essential air transport where free-market airline economics fail.
slides.technical_callout: Model Equation: Ci = Sum((Fij * Sij / sqrt(Tij)) * Whub,j)
slides.speaker_notes: We quantify connectivity using the ACI formula. Hub multipliers ensure that connections to major intercontinental gateways carry higher strategic weight.

slides.title: The Core Ecosystem Stakeholders & Regulatory Interfaces
slides.subtitle: How airlines, aerodromes, and ANSPs integrate to execute a flight
slides.key_takeaway: No individual flight departs through the actions of an airline alone; it requires the convergence of five primary regulated stakeholder domains.
bullets: Airlines (AOC Holders): ICAO Annex 6 / EASA Part-CAT for operational control, dispatch, and commercial execution.
Aerodromes (ADR): ICAO Annex 14 / EASA Part-ADR for runways, taxiways, obstacle clearance, and RFFS.
ANSPs (Air Traffic): ICAO Annex 11 / EASA Part-ATM/ANS for air traffic control, airspace management, and flow management (ATFM).
MRO & Ground Handling: Continuing airworthiness (CAMO/Part-145) and ramp turnaround services.
slides.technical_callout: Regulatory Hierarchy: ICAO SARPs -> EU Basic Reg -> EASA Implementing Rules -> National Aviation Authority oversight.
slides.speaker_notes: A flight relies on tight coordination between airlines, aerodromes, ANSPs, and maintenance providers under strict regulatory oversight.
